title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?

population.description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems

intervention.description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)

comparator.description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
comparator.definition: Soil mechanically disturbed before planting using plow, disk, or similar implements

primary.description: Crop grain yield per unit area
primary.direction_of_interest: either (no-till can increase or decrease yield depending on crop/climate)

intervention: No-till or zero-till (direct seeding without soil disturbance)
control: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, or inversion tillage)
typical_effect_size: -5.7% overall, varies by crop: wheat -2.6%, maize -7.6%, rice -7.5%, soybean +0.3%
important_moderators: Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, barley, sorghum, cotton, etc.)
Soil type or texture (clay, loam, sand)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY crop-year-site combination separately
2. Treatment = NO-TILL; Control = CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (most intensive tillage in the study)
3. If multiple crops tested, extract EACH crop vs control
4. If reduced tillage AND no-till both present, extract no-till vs conventional (not reduced vs conventional)
6. Record crop species and years since no-till adoption
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately

search.seed_papers_description: Pittelkow et al. 2015 (Nature, global meta-analysis of no-till), Van den Putte et al. 2010, Derpsch et al. 2014

inclusion_criteria: Primary field experiment comparing no-till to conventional tillage
No-till treatment has no or minimal soil disturbance at planting
Conventional tillage uses moldboard plow, disk, or similar
exclusion_criteria: Only reduced tillage, no true no-till treatment

published_pooled_effect.notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%
